title: Ops sprint release brief and calendaring — March 2026 (WIP)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This brief is a working ops-focused release plan for the upcoming March sprint window. It combines a compact preflight checklist, a day-by-day calendar for the cutover week, and a release notes draft to be handed to product, support, and customer success. Intended audience: release engineering, SRE on-call, product PM, solutions/SEs for customer comms.

High-level release window:
- Release block: 2026-03-15 00:00 UTC to 2026-03-16 08:00 UTC (target cutover starts 03-15 01:00 UTC)
- Expected traffic impact: <2% traffic routing shift to fallback for first 10 minutes, full traffic by +30m if green
- Blackout window: no user-facing schema migrations between 2026-03-14 12:00 UTC and 2026-03-16 12:00 UTC

Primary owners and contacts:
- Release lead: Maya Chen (Slack: @maya) — overall coordination, go/no-go calls
- SRE lead: Diego Alvarez (Slack: @diego) — infra readiness, autoscaler checks
- Product PM: Priya Nair (Slack: @priya) — release notes and feature prioritization
- QA / Smoke lead: Zoe Park (Slack: @zoe) — smoke tests and gating
- On-call escalation: SRE pager rotation (see oncall roster link in Confluence)

Preflight checklist (to be completed 48–24 hours before start):
- [ ] Finalize release notes draft and circulate to Support (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Confirm canary cluster capacity + pre-warmed instances (owner: Diego)
- [ ] Run the automated preflight tests on staging with production-like data sample (owner: Zoe)
- [ ] Verify model artifact checksum and manifest in artifact store (owner: eng-serving-runtime release lead)
- [ ] Lock down schema migrations and add DB feature flags if needed (owner: platform-eng)
- [ ] Confirm rollback images/versions are available and tested (owner: release-engineering)
- [ ] Ensure logging and tracing retention for +72 hours after cutover (owner: observability)
- [ ] Notify partner teams and any customers on the scheduled list (owner: solutions-eng)

Cutover checklist (step-by-step for the 03-15 window):
- T-minus 60m: Release lead opens the call, confirm all owners on call, run preflight status (Maya)
- T-minus 30m: Freeze non-essential PR merges, ensure CI runners are idle (Release engineering)
- T-minus 15m: Start small canary deployment to 5% of traffic and run smoke suite (Zoe)
- T-plus 0m: Monitor canary metrics for 10m: error rate, 95th latency, token throughput, memory OOMs (SRE)
- T-plus 10m: If metrics stable, ramp to 25% and run extended eval set (release eng + ML infra)
- T-plus 30m: Ramp to 100% if green, begin post-cutover validations across regions (Release lead + SRE)
- If at any point error rate >1.0% absolute increase, or 95p latency > baseline + 150ms, execute rollback plan (see below)

Rollback / abort criteria and quick steps:
- Immediate abort criteria: 5xx spike >3x baseline, persistent JVM OOMs on >2 nodes, or KV cache corruption errors
- Safe rollback steps (high-level):
  1) Signal abort on call, pause traffic ramping (Release lead)
  2) Switch traffic to previous stable model variant in routing service (SRE)
  3) Re-deploy verified previous images to canary and prod pools (release engineering)
  4) Clear in-flight caches only if necessary and safe (ML infra)
  5) Open incident channel and assign triage leads (SRE + release eng)
- Post-rollback actions: collect logs, capture core dumps, re-run staging reproducer, schedule deep-dive

Monitoring and smoke checks (first 3 hours):
- Critical: 5xx count, client error ratio, 95th token-generation latency, avg tokens/s per GPU
- Secondary: model-quality sanity checks from eval harness (top-k sampling similarity), embedding drift checks
- Health endpoints: model-server /health, KV cache /metrics, autoscaler /status
- Run smoke script: rle-smoke.sh --warmup 60 --testset smoke-50 (Zoe to kick off)

Post-release tasks (first 48 hours):
- [ ] Collect and publish token-level cost delta for the release (owner: finance-ops)
- [ ] Push final release notes and customer-facing blurb to GTM (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Run nightly regressions on canary subset for 3 days (owner: QA)
- [ ] Archive temporary debug logs to S3 and mark retention (observability)
- [ ] Schedule postmortem debrief if any gating alerts fired (release lead)

Quick reference calendar (local times shown UTC):
- 2026-03-13: Final signoff meeting (15:00 UTC) — owners to confirm preflight checklist
- 2026-03-14: Dry-run on staging (08:00–10:00 UTC) — full smoke + scale tests
- 2026-03-15: Cutover window (00:00–08:00 UTC) — live deployment and ramping steps
- 2026-03-16: Post-release validations and monitoring (00:00–12:00 UTC) — daily reports

Risk notes and mitigations:
- Risk: autoscaler misfires under burst traffic. Mitigation: pre-warm instances and set temporary floor of N+2 nodes during window (SRE).
- Risk: regression in streaming responses increases latency. Mitigation: use traffic shaping to route small proportion to canary and keep streaming timeout conservative.
- Risk: rollback introduces cache inconsistencies. Mitigation: have cache flush playbook and short TTLs for prefix cache during rollout (ML infra).

Draft release notes (to be iterated with product and comms):
Title: "March 2026 runtime optimizations and routing improvements"
Short blurb (customer-facing):
We rolled out a set of server-side runtime optimizations that reduce tail latency for text generation and improve routing resilience across regions. Users should see faster responses for long-form generation and fewer transient errors during high throughput bursts. No client changes required.
What's new (bullet):
- Optimized KV cache eviction logic for large context windows (RLE-834)
- Routing fallback: new model-variant policy reduces cross-region failovers
- Autoscaler tuning to reduce spin-up latency for sudden traffic spikes
Fixes and internal changes (engineers):
- Fixed a rare OOM during sequence concatenation (PR #4821)
- Resolved a race in the continuous batching scheduler that could cause token-order jitter
End-user impact and migration notes:
- No action required from customers. Backwards-compatible rollout.
Known issues (tracked):
- Small subset of legacy clients may see increased cold-start latency until caches prime (tracking: RLE-842)
- Some internal monitoring alerts may fire as thresholds adjust; these are informational during first 24 hours

Open questions / TODOs (next edits):
- Confirm exact blackout contact list and timezone conversions for APAC oncall (Priya)
- Verify the linear ticket RLE-834 has full test coverage for large contexts (Diego)
- Finalize comms blurb for customers with enterprise SLAs (Solutions Eng)

Appendix: useful commands and quick links:
- Promote canary: infractl rollout promote --target=canary --version=v2026.03.15
- Rollback: infractl rollout rollback --target=prod --to-version=v2026.03.01
- Smoke run: ./scripts/rle-smoke.sh --env=prod-canary --tests=smoke-50
- Confluence: confluence:release-annotations-2026-march
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821
- Linear: https://linear.app/RLE/issue/RLE-834-fleet-scaling-fix

---
Notes: keep this doc lightweight; move finalized call minutes and full postmortem to Confluence page after release.
